findings.title: Pagination params are unbounded and unvalidated
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` has no upper bound. A client can send `limit=10000000` and force the server to load and serialize every member of a large group. A negative `limit` or `offset` is passed straight to SQL, and PostgreSQL errors on a negative LIMIT or OFFSET, which returns a 500. The old code at least limited the result for automatic groups. Clamp `limit` to a maximum (e.g. 1..200) and `offset` to >= 0.

findings.title: Public members endpoint changes its response shape and default size
findings.body: `GET /groups/:name/members` used to return a bare JSON array, unpaginated for non-automatic groups. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {...}}` and silently caps results at 50 for every group. Any other client of this endpoint, such as plugins, other JS code or API users, will break or silently see a truncated list. The change is not documented, and no spec covers the new `members` action's shape, limit, offset or meta.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 pages for exactly 50 members at limit 50, and 3 for 100. The last page is therefore empty. `showingLast` stays false on the real last page, so "next" is still enabled. `next` then sets `offset = min(offset+limit, user_count)`, which equals `user_count`, and loads an empty page. It should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Username input is never cleared and is not reset between groups
findings.body: After `addMembers`, `usernames` stays set. Clicking Add again re-sends the same users, and the old value can persist when the controller is reused for another group. The code has a TODO acknowledging this but ships it. The result of `addMembers` is also not handled, so a failed request gives the user no feedback.

findings.title: Reload after removal can leave the user on an empty page
findings.body: `removeMember` and `addMembers` call `findMembers()` with the current offset. If the last member of the last page is removed, `offset` still points past the end (the clamp is only against `user_count`, which is stale until the response arrives). The admin sees an empty list and a wrong page indicator. Neither method has an error handler.

findings.title: Spec uses the wrong HTTP verb and misses key cases
findings.body: The route for `remove_member` is DELETE, but the automatic-group test uses `xhr :put, :remove_member`. It passes only because controller specs do not enforce the verb. There are also no tests for removing a non-member, adding non-existent usernames, or the new paginated `GroupsController#members` response. The old tests for those cases (silent success on unknown users) were deleted without replacement.
